design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (farm_real_estate_servicing).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5]}. Root farmland_ext_farmstead_release_price takes 5 factors, farmland_ext_missed_late_charge 5, farmland_ext_split_paydown 4.
[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: farmland_ext_default_interest_entry (book_default_interest_ef623284) and farmland_ext_autopay_enrolment_rate (authorize_installment_autodebit_3b801ea5). Claimed here: the late charge (farmland_fee_assessed, assess_late_charge_e3cbcc6c, agent), the member's split paydown (farmland_principal_payment, authorize_principal_paydown_4d1911cd, owner user) and the farmstead release price (farmland_parcel_released, release_farmstead_parcel_0569f2e2, agent). These are three base events task 0 never writes; together the two tasks cover all five extended policies with disjoint tools. No headroom is reserved: M = 2 and this is the last task.
[Why a good test] Dwight asks only to have the homesite released. The release price is a premium on the homesite's share of principal whose premium has four record-driven additions and whose homesite value turns on a Country Home application in another product; the release itself is not allowed until principal, less the standard release price, is within a post-split limit built from three ladders (operating leverage, collateral mix, crop insurance) plus a curtailment keyed to the home financing, and the premium waits on a late charge that should have been assessed on the September installment. Discovery is from prerequisite sentences and records; arithmetic is in each of the three computations.
[Problem-tree card] Root A1 = farmland_ext_farmstead_release_price. Edge A1 -> B1 farmland_ext_split_paydown: kind state_gate, gate farmland_loans.principal_balance, form state, sentence (negated direction, as a release desk states that a release waits for a standing condition): "A homesite release is not recorded until the principal standing on the loan, less the release price at the product's standard release premium on the homesite's appraised value at mortgage, already sits within the post-split loan-to-value limit of the parcels that stay mortgaged." Edge A1 -> C1 farmland_ext_missed_late_charge: kind value_input, gate record_add, form state, sentence (affirmative, as a price is fixed after its inputs stand): "The release price is set only once the records carry the late charge owed on every installment that was paid in full after its grace period." Four-point test, both: ordering connective ("not ... until", "only once"); waited-on side a record-visible state (principal on the loan; a late charge standing), no action named; no tool, id or code token; scope equals the condition field. One write each: principal falls below the limit only through a principal prepayment - the member's paydown tool is the only writer of payment_purpose prepayment in this difficulty (the release's own proceeds come after); a late-charge fee row is written only by assess_late_charge_e3cbcc6c. The charter's prerequisite sentences run in both directions (task 0 and the late-charge edge affirmative, the release edge negated). Unmet at frozen_time: principal 1,635,486.53 against a most of 1,622,431.13 (68.04 percent after the standard release price against the 67.5 percent limit); bill row due 2026-09-04, completing payment 2026-09-22, no late-charge row, fees_due 0.00. Resolution order C1, B1, A1; C1 and B1 commute (each reads nothing the other writes). Deletion sensitivity (run): without C1 the release price is 267,383.42 instead of 288,774.10; without B1 it is 292,932.02 and terminal principal 1,342,554.51 instead of 1,323,498.12. The customer's own write is B1 (paying principal from his own checking account); it completes on the spot.
[Base-invariant card] C1 (farmland_fee_assessed): farmland_evt_late_charge gates inherited - time gate farmland_late_after_grace (anchor farmland_transactions.due_date 2026-09-04, 15 calendar days, due date day 0, exclusive: arises 2026-09-20; boundary 2026-09-19 not yet), dedup farmland_one_late_charge (no late charge on that bill); the other seven fee policies govern other fee kinds (policy_scope). Its percentage sentence is superseded by the declared overwrite; the min/max bounds are kept. B1 (farmland_principal_payment): farmland_accepts_payments (status active), farmland_prepayment (variable product, empty schedule: no fee), farmland_partial_release (scope). A1 (farmland_parcel_released): release_loan_status (active), parcel_released_once (Tract A has no release row), farmland_agg_combined_ltv (one farm loan - same as the loan test), farmland_payoff (scope); the base release-price sentence is superseded by the declared overwrite (premium additions and homesite valuation). No installment is past due at frozen_time (next due 2027-03-04), so no partial-release or prepayment bar applies.
[Business-object card] Loan: the member's FarmLand Variable-Rate Mortgage (opened 2023-03-04, 1,720,000.00). Homesite: mortgage record of parcel 300518412, Tract A of a recorded survey, 7.50 acres, farmstead, 268,000.00; named by the submitted partial_release request of 2026-10-13. Late charge object: the bill row with period_end 2026-09-04 (the bill is split into three rows at the 2026-04-30 and 2026-07-30 base-rate changes; the payments point to the last row). Excluded: the 2024-06-17 condemnation of the highway strip (no fee, counted only in the release history), earlier on-time installments.
[Factor card - C1, amount 85.90] late_charge_percentage_by_record 3.0 (no late charge in 36 months, 42 months old; baseline 4.0 -> 154.62); good_faith_payment_credit 1.0 (60,490.62 interest paid 2026-09-10 inside grace, more than half the installment; baseline 0 -> 154.62); operating_relationship_credit 0.25 (Revolving Operating Line active on AutoDraft, cross-difficulty; baseline 0 -> 103.08); crop_season_credit 0.5 (September; baseline 0 -> 120.26); lateness_multiplier one half (completed in 18 days; baseline 1 -> 171.80). Fall-back 549.77.
[Factor card - B1, amount 23,214.31] limit_by_operating_leverage -5.0 (83.5 percent drawn, cross-difficulty, multi-source; baseline -> 10,158.91); limit_by_collateral_mix -5.0 (pasture 30.4 percent of what stays; near-miss: the released strip; baseline -> 10,158.91); limit_by_crop_insurance +2.5 (assigned 2026 corn policy, cross-difficulty, multi-source; baseline -> 83,304.35); split_curtailment_by_home_financing (method, cross-difficulty homeloan, multi-source) 5 percent of 203,178.01 = 10,158.9007 because the application is 83.2 percent of the stated value (baseline shortfall alone -> 13,055.40). Fall-back 0.00 (no paydown).
[Factor card - A1, release_price 288,774.10] premium_by_late_record +10.0 (one late charge in 24 months, the prerequisite's; baseline -> 267,383.42); premium_by_homesite_size +5.0 (7.50 acres; -> 278,078.76); premium_by_release_history +5.0 (one release in 60 months; -> 278,078.76); premium_by_loan_seasoning +5.0 (43 months; -> 278,078.76); homesite_value_by_newest_appraisal (method, cross-difficulty homeloan, multi-source) greater of 268,000.00 and the 322,000.00 stated in the application received 2026-09-28 (-> 245,815.47). Fall-back 200,294.08. Every premium tier is at or above the standard premium and the homesite value is never below its value at mortgage, so the actual release price is never below the standard one the paydown counts: after the release principal is 1,323,498.12 against a limit of 1,420,875.00.
[Rows] Customer (phone 4024637415, CPF-3582204, 6128). Loan. Six parcel rows (five mortgaged, one condemnation release). Twenty-seven transactions: seven installment bills (three split), their interest and principal payments, the condemnation proceeds. Two partial-release requests. Revolving Operating Line (active, 334,000.00 of 400,000.00, AutoDraft, account 3164). Two 2026 crop policies (corn assigned, soybeans not). One Country Home application on the homesite. Removing the September payment rows removes the late charge; removing the application removes the curtailment tier and the value uplift; removing the operating line removes the leverage cut and the relationship credit.
[Persona] Dwight Halvorsen, terse, calling from the combine; raises only the homesite release; credentials and the tract only when asked; accepts a late charge with an admission about harvest; runs the paydown himself from the account ending 3164 when handed it; accepts the release price; ends when told the homesite is released. He asks for nothing else and cannot check numbers.
[Standard solution] locate, verify, read loan, requests, transactions, parcels, operating line, crop policies, home loan application; assess the late charge (85.90 on the bill row of 2026-09-04); hand over the paydown (23,214.31 from 3164); release Tract A with release price 288,774.10 and fee 350.00.
[Verification] check_compute --task 1 COMPUTE OK (85.90, 23,214.31 and 288,774.10 recomputed at handling time; every factor baseline moves the result; value_input edge re-run without the late charge gives 267,383.42); check_extended, check_solvability, check_grounding, check_cross_fire, check_task_tools OK; replay deterministic with only the coordinator-accepted loan_id foreign-key line.
[Revisions] Symptom: compute gate reported the late charge's history as not load-bearing -> root cause: the interest paid was read with LATEST, which the zeroing test does not touch, and the only COUNT was already zero -> change: the interest paid is now the sum of interest payments pointing to the bill row, and the rule says so -> re-run COMPUTE OK. Symptom: the release prerequisite sentence ("once the release price is applied") would let a reader apply the actual 135 percent premium and find the state already met -> change: the sentence now names the release price at the product's standard premium, the measure the paydown rule uses -> unique reading. First sensitivity fill ran with zero gold amounts and was re-run to a fixed point.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules: the late charge rule gives 13,744.20 x 1.25 percent x 0.5 = 85.90; the paydown rule gives limit 67.5, most principal 1,622,431.13, shortfall 13,055.3997 plus 10,158.9007 curtailment = 23,214.3004, rounded up once to 23,214.31; the release rule then gives 135 percent of 213,906.74 = 288,774.10. The late charge and the paydown may be written in either order with the same result.
[Revisions, round 2 - audit closure] F-1: the paydown compute used -int(-x) as a ceiling, which truncates (floors) for a positive x, and the rule left open whether the round-up came before or after the curtailment. The rule now says the curtailment is added to the shortfall before any rounding and the sum is rounded up to the next cent once, neither part rounded on its own; compute takes cents_due = (shortfall + curtailment) x 100 and adds one cent when it has any fraction. Gold paydown 23,214.30 -> 23,214.31 (13,055.3997 + 10,158.9007 = 23,214.3004 rounded up); principal after the paydown 1,612,272.22; terminal principal 1,323,498.12; the release price stays 288,774.10 (share 213,906.74 either way); factor figures re-run exactly: leverage and mix baselines 10,158.91, crop insurance 83,304.35, curtailment baseline 13,055.40, fall-back 0.00. O-2: the release prerequisite sentence and condition now name the homesite at its appraised value at mortgage, the measure the paydown rule uses, so the gate cannot be read as already met with the 322,000.00 application value. O-4: the paydown rule no longer restates the order ('before the release' removed); its first sentence now names the shortfall and the curtailment only. O-7: the good-faith credit now speaks of the interest paid on the installment within the grace period, which is what compute counts. O-8: the paydown overwrite now supersedes only the clause from 'after which principal may not exceed ...', so 'The release price is applied to principal as release proceeds on the release date' stays inherited; the prepayment-fee gap on products with a schedule does not arise on this variable-rate world. O-3, O-10 and O-11 were examined and need no change: the state gate is carried by the prerequisite sentence as the framework intends, the semantic multi-source floor is met by the good-faith credit, the operating leverage and the homesite value, and no rule gates the release on the request status.
user_scenario: You are Dwight Halvorsen, a corn, soybean and cow-calf farmer near Geneva in Fillmore County, Nebraska. You are calling the Cottonwood Plains Farm Credit servicing desk from the cab of the combine during a fuel stop, so you speak in short, practical sentences and like to get to the point. You and your family are building a Country Home loan on the farmstead: the house and yard on Tract A, parcel 300518412, the seven and a half acres the house sits on. The co-op's home loan people need that tract out from under your farm mortgage before they can put the house loan on it, and you turned in the paperwork asking for it at the Geneva branch last Tuesday. What you want from this call is simple: get the homesite released from the farm mortgage today so the house loan can go ahead. You don't know how the co-op figures what the release costs and you don't pretend to. You only give details when asked. Your phone number is 4024637415. If the agent wants more to be sure it's you, you give your membership number, CPF-3582204, and the last four of your social, 6128. If asked which tract, it's Tract A, parcel 300518412; you have just the one farm mortgage. The co-op's own bookkeeping and the release itself you leave to the agent. Anything that comes out of your own bank account you want to authorise yourself: if the agent tells you a principal payment has to be made from your side first, you say you have savings set aside for this, ask them to hand you whatever you need to approve, and you run it with the amount they give you, out of the checking account ending 3164, and read back the confirmation. If the agent tells you a late charge is owed, you admit the September payment went in a couple of weeks late in the middle of harvest and say if it's owed, put it on. When they tell you the release price, you say that's what the house loan is for and that's fine. You don't ask for anything else - not a letter, not a payoff figure, nothing about the house loan itself. Once the agent says the homesite has been released from the farm mortgage, you thank them and hang up to get back to the field. You have no statements with you, so if a number is mentioned you cannot check it and simply take the agent's word.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel and commute. The late charge reads the latest bill, the interest paid on it, the latest scheduled principal payment, the late-charge count and the operating line; the paydown adds a principal row with payment_purpose prepayment, which none of those reads selects, so the charge is 85.90 either way. The paydown reads the parcels, the principal balance, the operating line, the crop insurance policies and the Country Home application; the late charge changes only fees_due and adds a fee row, which none of those reads selects, so the paydown is 23,214.31 either way. Writing late charge then paydown, or paydown then late charge, gives the same rows and the same loan fields. The release must follow both: its own sentences ('not recorded until the principal ... already sits within the post-split ... limit' and 'set only once the records carry the late charge owed ...') place it after each.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the late charge leaves no late-charge row and fees_due at 350.00 instead of 435.90 after the release; the release price recomputed without it is 267,383.42 instead of 288,774.10 (record addition none instead of 10.0 points), so principal after the release differs by 21,390.68.

Skipping the paydown leaves no prepayment row and principal 1,635,486.53 at the release; the release price on that principal is 292,932.02 instead of 288,774.10, and the terminal principal is 1,342,554.51 instead of 1,323,498.12; the release would also be recorded while the standard-premium test fails (68.04 percent against the 67.5 percent limit).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: Dwight asks only to have the homesite released from the farm mortgage so it can go on the house loan. He never mentions the September installment, its timing, a late charge, a paydown, a loan-to-value limit or the operating line's balance; his only words about money are that he has savings set aside and will move whatever the co-op says it needs, which he says only after the agent explains that a paydown is required. A late charge reaches him only as a passive explanation he accepts.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: release_farmstead_parcel_0569f2e2 writes the release row, the release-proceeds payment, the fee and the loan balances with whatever price it is given; it never checks the principal against any limit or looks for late charges. authorize_principal_paydown_4d1911cd and assess_late_charge_e3cbcc6c likewise book exactly what they are given. An agent that skips either prerequisite still releases the homesite successfully and is caught only by the terminal hash.
